title: Strengthened upper bound on the third eigenvalue of graphs: the block construction is optimal
author: Sida Li
work: Strengthened upper bound on the third eigenvalue of graphs
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's Theorem (source0.tex lines 801--803, source label thm:block): if G is the closed vertex multiplication of the six-cycle by the block pattern with parameters a, b, c, a, b, c, then the sum of the second and third largest eigenvalues of G is at most two thirds of the number of vertices minus two, with equality exactly in the stated case; delivered with the article's complete original proof at source0.tex lines 804--830 (one adjacent proof environment of 27 lines that opens and closes inside the retained span). The proof is complete and closed inside the retained span and uses nothing outside the statement. It adds a self-loop at every vertex, writes the divisor matrix of the equitable partition of the resulting graph, computes the characteristic polynomial of that matrix and factors it into a quadratic factor and a cubic factor, identifies the eigenvalues of the graph with the regularity eigenvalue and the roots of the cubic, normalises the block parameters, substitutes a root of the form one third plus t into the cubic, derives the sign identity for the cubic at one third minus t, concludes that one third plus t must be the smallest root so that the sum of the two smallest roots is bounded by two thirds, and finally translates the bound back to the two largest eigenvalues of the graph together with its equality case. The theorem is the optimality statement for the block construction that appears in the proof of the article's main bound on the third eigenvalue, so it is a genuine research-level spectral graph theory result. H2: a research-level spectral-graph-theory theorem whose proof combines equitable partitions and divisor matrices, an explicit characteristic-polynomial factorisation and a root-location argument for a cubic; it is well beyond ordinary PhD qualifying exercises.
